title: IC: communications, records, operations and offline work
summary: Communicate within the incident, document work, manage the command device and verify offline replay.
prerequisites: Chat.System, actual incident/lane channels and assistant service configured.
Reachable LiveKit and voice session services, microphone permission and a second authorized endpoint.
Records.System and Records.Field.IncidentCommand enabled with supported records and assignments; prepared connectors and deployments.
Operations.Deployments and applicable finance/costing/MARS access; shared-session and account-security configuration.
Hydrate the session, board and references online before offline capture; use a native build for BLE, CallKeep, camera, critical alerts and background behavior.

scenes.title: Incident voice and transmission history
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: In Voice Channels, add a permitted incident channel using a preset or a clear name. Join the channel and use the microphone control to change its state, then Leave when the exchange is finished. Inspect Transmission Log and its page controls when recorded transmissions exist. Close All ends the incident’s channels when appropriate. Verify real audio reception on another training endpoint before claiming it worked. The browser uses WebRTC and still needs permission and a reachable voice service. Native Bluetooth hardware, operating-system call handling and background audio require separate native footage; the visible browser controls do not demonstrate those capabilities.
scenes.practice: Create a tactical training channel, conduct a verified short exchange and inspect the available transmission history.
capture_observations: Voice setup still needs capture. No audio transmission, native hardware or external provider test performed.

scenes.title: Command chat, direct messages and assistant
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Use Command, All Leads, Dispatch or the lane’s chat action to open the intended conversation. A channel may still be loading or may not have been created, so read an unavailable or retry message honestly. Role-holder and lane-lead message actions provide more focused communication. Message Commander on the call offers a subject, body and optional deputy recipients through the configured notification channels. The incident assistant can use a focused question or suggestion, but its response still needs review against the actual board and department guidance. A notification, chat reply and assistant answer are different workflows; verify each through its own returned state.
scenes.practice: Ask for an event medical update in the relevant channel, then draft a message to the commander.
capture_observations: Internal app chat authorized but not attempted before browser interruption. No message delivery claimed.

scenes.title: Text conversation, threads and notification delivery
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Open Chat to choose a direct conversation, channel or incident discussion, or create a permitted group. Compose text, an image, GIF or location where allowed. Urgent messaging introduces acknowledgment; use a second participant to demonstrate that action. Message actions can include reply, copy, edit, delete, pin or flag depending on permissions, and threads keep replies attached to their original message. Archived incident conversations can remain readable while posting is frozen. The app-header notification inbox and operating-system push need their own demonstration. Browser push requires permission, Firebase configuration and a service worker, while native critical-alert behavior must be captured on a properly configured device.
scenes.practice: Send a SAR coordination message, reply in its thread and complete a real training acknowledgment.
capture_observations: Chat/threads/notifications not captured; no send, acknowledgment or push delivery claimed.

scenes.title: Field records and attachments
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Open Records to inspect assigned work, drafts, returned items and recent records. Acknowledge an assignment where offered, then choose the permitted definition or start New Record from a useful incident context. Review prefilled values, complete required fields and repeating rows, and add approved photo or file attachments. The definition decides whether Keep on this device is offered or an online Save and send is required. Reopen and Save a draft before Submit for review, or complete the required attestation for an authorized Finalize. Unsupported definitions and online-only records need their stated workflow; the presence of an offline board does not make every record available offline.
scenes.practice: Create a fictional industrial incident record, attach a training image and inspect its allowed submission path.
capture_observations: Records list/definition/form still need capture; no record submitted.

scenes.title: Record deployments, connectors and operations
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Records deployment screens show source snapshots, fills, linked artifacts and reconciliation information. Connector details explain authority, readiness and run history; Read feed now is a real backend operation; the screen explains that connector administration and credentials are managed on the web. Open Deployments from navigation, then select the deployment, date and roster scope before creating individual or crew time. Review time type, start and end, breaks and other applicable details, then Save and Submit report. Signatures and approval depend on role and state. Add expenses and receipts where permitted, record enabled resource usage, and inspect F-42 validation when MARS is configured. Finance mode can hide numbers or panels; do not imply reimbursement or external acceptance from their presence.
scenes.practice: Review a wildland crew day, add one training expense and inspect an imported deployment discrepancy.
capture_observations: The observed navigation label is Deployments. Deployment/time/expense/connector screens still need capture; no financial action performed.

scenes.title: Preferences, account security and platform differences
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: In Settings, verify the app version, environment and server, then inspect Login Info without exposing credentials. Theme, language and keep-awake preferences prepare the command surface. The BT Handset control belongs to a supported native device and available hardware; record its actual connection flow there. Open Sign-in and security to review methods, passkeys, approval preferences and account activity. Adding or changing a passkey needs the real platform authenticator and verification process. Shared device configures the installation, while server session controls manage its shift and lock. Support and status links open external information. Use the device’s actual options instead of presenting a browser recording as native parity.
scenes.practice: Prepare a security command tablet’s language and keep-awake settings, then locate its security activity view.
capture_observations: Account and preferences screens captured. Login Info was not opened to avoid credential exposure; no passkey/MFA/password or hardware changes made.

scenes.title: Work offline and inspect the queue
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Begin online so the app has the authorized session, board and reference information. Disconnect deliberately, make a supported practice change and inspect the pending-sync indication. In Settings, open View Sync Queue to inspect pending, processing, failed or completed events and their attempts. Reconnect and use Sync Now, then verify the resulting board from another client. Retry Failed or an individual retry is appropriate only when that state actually exists. Canceling an event or clearing the queue changes what can be replayed, so reserve those controls for disposable exercises. Queued and failed events are not server-confirmed actions, and a reconnect alone does not prove replay succeeded.
scenes.practice: Make a harmless SAR board change offline, reconnect and verify the accepted result on a second client.
capture_observations: Settings Sync & Offline Queue entry captured. Queue detail and actual offline replay have not been demonstrated.

scenes.title: Finish the working session deliberately
scenes.capture_intent: Record the named screen and the described controls with prepared training data; verify the actual visible permissions and returned state before describing the action.
scenes.narration: Before handing over, review the board’s current incident, unresolved needs and synchronization state. An incident command transfer should use Transfer on the board; changing operators on a shared device is a separate session action. Use Lock for an unattended supported shared session or End Shift when the operator’s shift is finished. Ordinary Logout has a confirmation and clears local app data, cached values and settings, so resolve pending work before choosing it. Record the real configured behavior on the target platform. End with a clear handover of responsibilities and known pending items rather than treating an empty screen or a closed application as proof that the incident is complete.
scenes.practice: Hand over a community-event command device, distinguishing command transfer, pending sync and operator sign-out.
capture_observations: No voluntary Logout, End Shift or command transfer completed. Old session returned to login automatically; fresh-session completion is unverified.
